source_text: Tunc dixit mihi frater meus: Domina soror, iam in magna dignatione es: tanta es ut postules uisionem et ostendatur tibi an passio sit an commeatus. Et ego quae me sciebam fabulari cum domino, cuius beneficia tanta experta eram, fidens repromisi ei dicens: Crastina die tibi renuntiabo. Et postulaui, et ostensum est mihi hoc. Uideo scalam aeream mirae longitudinis, pertingentem usque ad caelum, et angustam, per quam nonnisi singuli ascendere possent; et in lateribus scalae omne genus ferramentorum infixum erat ibi: gladii, lanceae, hami, macherae, ueruta: ut, si quis neglegenter aut non sursum adtendens ascenderet, laniaretur et carnes eius inhaererent ferramentis. Et erat sub ipsa scala draco cubans mirae magnitudinis, qui ascendentibus insidias praestabat et exterrebat ne ascenderent. Ascendit autem Saturus prior, qui postea se propter nos ultro tradiderat, quia ipse nos aedificauerat; et tunc cum adducti sumus praesens non fuerat. Et peruenit in caput scalae, et conuertit se et dixit mihi: Perpetua, sustineo te; sed uide ne te mordeat draco ille. Et dixi ego: Non me nocebit, in nomine Iesu Christi. Et desub ipsa scala, quasi timens me, lente eiecit caput; et quasi primum gradum calcarem, calcaui illi caput, et ascendi. Et uidi spatium immensum horti, et in medio sedentem hominem canum in habitu pastoris, grandem, oues mulgentem: et circumstantes candidati milia multa. Et leuauit caput et aspexit me et dixit mihi: Bene uenisti, tegnon. Et clamauit me, et de caseo quod mulgebat dedit mihi quasi buccellam; et ego accepi iunctis manibus et manducaui; et uniuersi circumstantes dixerunt: Amen. Et ad sonum uocis experrecta sum, commanducans adhuc dulce nescio quid. Et retuli statim fratri meo, et intelleximus passionem esse futuram; et coepi iam nullam spem in saeculo habere.
pass_a_gloss: Literal sense: my brother called me honored lady and said I am in such favor that I may ask for a vision to be shown whether this is suffering-death or release; I, knowing I conversed with the Lord whose great benefits I had experienced, confidently promised to report next day; I asked and this was shown: I see a bronze ladder of wondrous length reaching to heaven and narrow so only single persons could climb, with every kind of iron weapon fixed on its sides — swords, spears, hooks, daggers, javelins — so that one climbing carelessly or not looking upward would be torn and his flesh would stick on the irons; under the ladder a dragon of wondrous size lay in wait to ambush climbers and frighten them from climbing; Saturus went up first, who afterwards had voluntarily surrendered himself on our account because he had instructed us, and had not been present when we were arrested; he reached the ladder top, turned and said, Perpetua, I await you, but beware lest that dragon bite you; I said, he will not harm me, in the name of Jesus Christ; from beneath the ladder as if fearing me it slowly thrust out its head, and as I set foot on the first rung I trod on its head and climbed; I saw an immense garden space and in the middle a white-haired man in shepherd dress, tall, milking sheep, with many thousands of white-clad ones standing around; he raised his head, looked at me, said, you have come well, child; he called me and gave me from the cheese he was milking as it were a mouthful; I received with joined hands and ate; all standing around said, Amen; at the sound of the voice I awoke, still chewing something sweet I know not what; I reported at once to my brother, we understood the coming event to be martyrdom, and I began now to have no hope in this world.
pass_b_english: Then my brother said to me, “My lady sister, you are now in great favor; you are so great that you may ask for a vision and it may be shown to you whether this is to be martyrdom or release.” And I, who knew that I spoke with the Lord, whose great benefits I had experienced, confidently promised him, saying, “Tomorrow I will report to you.” And I asked, and this was shown to me. I see a bronze ladder of wondrous length, reaching all the way to heaven (Genesis 28:12), and narrow, by which only single persons could ascend; and on the sides of the ladder every kind of iron weapon was fixed there: swords, spears, hooks, daggers, javelins, so that if anyone climbed carelessly or without looking upward, he would be torn and his flesh would cling to the irons. And beneath the ladder itself a dragon of wondrous size lay crouching, laying ambush for those ascending and frightening them lest they ascend. But Saturus ascended first, who afterward voluntarily handed himself over for our sake, because he himself had instructed us; and he had not been present when we were arrested. And he reached the head of the ladder, and he turned and said to me, “Perpetua, I am waiting for you; but see that that dragon does not bite you.” And I said, “He will not harm me, in the name of Jesus Christ.” And from beneath the ladder itself, as if fearing me, it slowly thrust out its head; and as I set foot on the first rung, I trod upon its head (Genesis 3:15), and I ascended.

And I saw an immense expanse of garden, and in the middle a white-haired man seated in shepherd’s dress, tall, milking sheep; and standing around were many thousands clad in white (Revelation 7:9). And he lifted his head and looked at me and said to me, “You have come well, child.” And he called me, and from the cheese which he was milking he gave me as it were a mouthful; and I received it with joined hands and ate it; and all those standing around said, “Amen.” And at the sound of the voice I awoke, still chewing something sweet I know not what. And I reported it at once to my brother, and we understood that the coming suffering was to be martyrdom; and I began now to have no hope in this world.

choices.english: whether it is to be martyrdom or release
choices.why: passio here is contextual martyrdom-suffering, not generic feeling, and commeatus is prison-release contrasted with it in the arrest narrative
rejected: whether it is passion or a journey

choices.why: first-person singular present addressed to Perpetua on the ladder-top, holding his place rather than enduring

choices.english: to the head of the ladder
choices.why: caput is the top end of the ladder just climbed, parallel to calcaui illi caput for the dragon
rejected: to the captain of the ladder
